professional_persona_scenarios.hidden_main_goal: Repurpose an old laptop into a reliable offline photo-backup and review station for future budget road trips.
professional_persona_scenarios.explicit_trigger: How can I check whether the hard drive in an old laptop is still healthy before I erase it?
implicit_anchors: Tho regularly imports large batches of DSLR photos from street-art and sunset shoots.
Tho prefers budget-friendly road trips and tries to reuse existing gear before buying replacements.
Tho is comfortable with hardware troubleshooting and basic scripting.

proactive_subtasks.task: Branch the diagnostic plan based on drive-health results.
proactive_subtasks.logic: The user cannot decide whether to reuse the laptop, replace the drive, or avoid relying on it until SMART checks and file-copy tests establish whether the current storage is trustworthy.

proactive_subtasks.task: Design an offline photo ingest and verification workflow.
proactive_subtasks.logic: If the laptop is going to hold DSLR shoots away from home, a working drive is not enough; the user also needs a repeatable copy-and-verify process to prevent silent file corruption.

proactive_subtasks.task: Add pre-trip reliability checks for power, ports, and storage headroom.
proactive_subtasks.logic: A healthy drive alone does not make the device usable during travel; battery behavior, charger condition, card-reader access, and free space determine whether the laptop can function as a dependable field station.

ideal_assistant_trajectory.description: Explain how to check drive health with SMART data if the laptop boots, how to use a bootable diagnostic tool if it does not, and how to run a practical read/write copy test before wiping anything.
Add that the user should verify copied files with checksums or another file-integrity method, because a simple boot test does not prove the laptop is safe for storing important media.
ideal_assistant_trajectory.grounding: Anchor: large batches of DSLR photos; implication: the user needs file-integrity protection, not only a basic drive status check.

ideal_assistant_trajectory.description: Propose a full reuse plan: if the drive and ports pass testing, reinstall a lightweight setup, create a clear import folder structure, and use the old laptop as an offline travel backup station instead of purchasing new gear.
ideal_assistant_trajectory.grounding: Anchors: large batches of DSLR photos + budget-friendly road trips + hardware troubleshooting; conclusion: the old laptop can be repurposed into a low-cost field backup and review device.

ideal_assistant_trajectory.description: After the core advice is complete, remind the user to copy off any remaining files before wiping the machine and to create one recovery installer or system image once the setup is stable.
ideal_assistant_trajectory.grounding: Detail: 'before I erase it'; action: preserve anything still on the laptop and make a recovery path before relying on the repurposed system.

professional_persona_scenarios.persona_alignment_check: All proactive subtasks stay within normal hardware-diagnostic practice, reuse existing equipment to respect budget limits, and avoid any unsafe or unethical activity.

ideal_assistant_trajectory.description: Propose a specific day plan: either eat the banh mi near the start of the session and carry only nonperishable snacks later, or pack a leakproof insulated pouch with a frozen water bottle and use sturdier, less messy items that fit alongside camera gear while staying within the cash limit.

ideal_assistant_trajectory.description: Offer a reusable outing packing checklist with separate zones for food and camera gear, plus a default rule for when to include an ice pack versus when to bring only shelf-stable items.
ideal_assistant_trajectory.grounding: Detail: "A DSLR is going in the same backpack for street-art photos afterward." Forward-looking action: create a repeatable bag-packing checklist that prevents food leaks near camera equipment.

travel_persona_scenarios.explicit_trigger: Help me tighten this list of oral-history interview questions for elders in coastal communities; I want them open-ended and easy to translate.
implicit_anchors: I will be moving between two coastal towns over four days and keeping everything in a carry-on.
I organize teaching materials in color-coded digital folders and reuse them later in class.
I already plan to take still photos and handwritten notes alongside any audio.

proactive_subtasks.task: Restructure the interview questions into a clear sequence with short follow-up probes.
proactive_subtasks.logic: A usable interview order is the first dependency for collecting consistent material across multiple conversations.

proactive_subtasks.task: Add a plain-language verbal consent script and a small metadata checklist for each interview.
proactive_subtasks.logic: Interview material is harder to use later unless each recording includes permission status, speaker details, date, and location.

proactive_subtasks.task: Propose a lightweight recording and file-naming workflow suited to carry-on travel.
proactive_subtasks.logic: Limited luggage and movement between towns make compact gear choices and disciplined file organization necessary.

proactive_subtasks.task: Create a nightly debrief template that links audio files, photos, and handwritten notes.
proactive_subtasks.logic: The user plans to collect material in multiple formats, so a cross-reference routine prevents fragments from becoming unusable later.

ideal_assistant_trajectory.description: Revise the user's interview questions into simpler, open-ended wording and organize them into a logical conversation flow.
Proactively suggest a standardized file-naming convention and folder structure for recordings and notes so the material remains usable after the trip.
ideal_assistant_trajectory.grounding: I organize teaching materials in color-coded digital folders and reuse them later in class -> unstated need: a structured archival system for travel-collected material.

ideal_assistant_trajectory.description: Recommend a lightweight field kit and a nightly cross-reference routine that connects each interview to the related photos and handwritten notes.
ideal_assistant_trajectory.grounding: I will be moving between two coastal towns over four days and keeping everything in a carry-on + I already plan to take still photos and handwritten notes alongside any audio -> conclusion: the user needs a compact multi-format capture workflow with a daily consolidation step.

ideal_assistant_trajectory.description: After finishing the questions, add a one-page interviewer card with short transition phrases and backup probe prompts in plain language for on-site use.
ideal_assistant_trajectory.grounding: easy to translate -> forward-looking action: prepare a simplified prompt sheet that reduces translation friction during live interviews.

culinary_persona_scenarios.hidden_main_goal: Design a safe refrigerate-freeze-assemble strategy for chiles en nogada components so the dish can be partially prepared before travel and finished after return without waste.
culinary_persona_scenarios.explicit_trigger: How long can roasted poblanos, picadillo filling, and walnut sauce stay in the refrigerator?
implicit_anchors: She leaves Thursday for a five-day trip to Carmel-by-the-Sea and returns Tuesday.
Wednesday afternoon is her only open prep window because of her evening folkloric dance workshop.
She already roasted six poblanos and has cream and walnut sauce ingredients in the refrigerator.

proactive_subtasks.task: Classify each component by whether it should be refrigerated, frozen, or delayed.
proactive_subtasks.logic: Shelf-life information alone is not enough; the user needs a storage decision for each component before leaving on the trip.

proactive_subtasks.task: Split the recipe into before-trip tasks and after-return tasks.
proactive_subtasks.logic: The single prep window and multi-day absence make a staged workflow necessary to complete the dish safely.

proactive_subtasks.task: Provide labeling and thawing instructions for the stored components.
proactive_subtasks.logic: Once components are frozen or delayed, the user needs dated labels and a return-day assembly sequence to finish the meal correctly.

ideal_assistant_trajectory.description: State the typical refrigerator life for roasted poblanos, cooked picadillo filling, and walnut sauce, noting that dairy-based sauce has the shortest safe window.
Point out that refrigerator storage alone will not cover the full absence for every component, so some parts should be frozen or postponed.
ideal_assistant_trajectory.grounding: Anchor: She leaves Thursday for a five-day trip to Carmel-by-the-Sea and returns Tuesday. Implication: the trip duration can exceed safe refrigerator storage for at least one prepared component.

ideal_assistant_trajectory.description: Recommend a split plan: freeze the roasted poblanos and picadillo after Wednesday prep, postpone the walnut sauce until after the trip or make only a very small batch, and reserve final stuffing and saucing for the return day.
ideal_assistant_trajectory.grounding: Anchors: She leaves Thursday for a five-day trip to Carmel-by-the-Sea and returns Tuesday; Wednesday afternoon is her only open prep window because of her evening folkloric dance workshop; She already roasted six poblanos and has cream and walnut sauce ingredients in the refrigerator. Conclusion: the recipe should be divided into freeze-now components and fresh-later components to fit the schedule and avoid spoilage.

ideal_assistant_trajectory.description: Add a short label set for the six poblanos and filling containers with dates, thaw timing, and the order for final assembly after the trip.
ideal_assistant_trajectory.grounding: Detail: She already roasted six poblanos. Forward-looking action: provide dated storage labels and a return-day thaw-and-assemble checklist.

culinary_persona_scenarios.hidden_main_goal: Turn perishable garden ingredients into safe, portioned meals and a packing plan for a two-night road trip with only motel mini-fridge storage.
culinary_persona_scenarios.explicit_trigger: How long will homemade vegetable stew stay good in the fridge and freezer if I cook it tomorrow?
implicit_anchors: A two-night road trip starts the day after cooking, with one budget motel stop that only has a mini-fridge.
The plan includes an early-morning prairie photography stop before breakfast on the first full day.
There are several ripe tomatoes to use soon, and the lettuce is already wilted from extra watering.

proactive_subtasks.task: Give safe fridge and freezer storage times plus basic cooling guidance for the stew.
proactive_subtasks.logic: Storage limits determine whether the stew can be used during the trip or frozen for later.

proactive_subtasks.task: Sort the available foods into eat-before-leaving, eat-on-day-one, and freeze-for-after-the-trip categories.
proactive_subtasks.logic: The mini-fridge and travel duration create different handling needs for fresh vegetables and cooked food.

proactive_subtasks.task: Build a compact packing plan for meals that works with the motel mini-fridge and the early departure schedule.
proactive_subtasks.logic: The trip setup limits storage space and reduces time available for morning food preparation.

ideal_assistant_trajectory.description: Answer how long vegetable stew keeps in the refrigerator and freezer, and include basic cooling and reheating guidance.
Suggest portioning the stew into smaller containers instead of storing one large pot.
ideal_assistant_trajectory.grounding: Anchor: 'A two-night road trip starts the day after cooking, with one budget motel stop that only has a mini-fridge.' Implication: storage space will be limited, so compact portions are needed.

ideal_assistant_trajectory.description: Recommend freezing most stew portions, using tomatoes early in the trip, skipping the wilted lettuce, and preparing a portable first-morning food option that does not require cooking.
ideal_assistant_trajectory.grounding: Anchors: 'A two-night road trip starts the day after cooking, with one budget motel stop that only has a mini-fridge.' + 'The plan includes an early-morning prairie photography stop before breakfast on the first full day.' + 'There are several ripe tomatoes to use soon, and the lettuce is already wilted from extra watering.' Conclusion: the food plan should favor frozen portions, immediate use of tomatoes, no lettuce-based meal, and a ready-to-eat morning item.

ideal_assistant_trajectory.description: After the storage advice, add a simple evening-before and departure-morning packing sequence for cooling, freezing, and loading the food.
ideal_assistant_trajectory.grounding: Detail: 'A two-night road trip starts the day after cooking.' Forward-looking action: provide a timed packing checklist for the night before and morning of departure.

culinary_persona_scenarios.hidden_main_goal: Design a safe, low-cost plan to use leftover mushroom and sage pot pie as a meal during a full day at a renovation site with no reliable cold storage.
culinary_persona_scenarios.explicit_trigger: How long can a cooked mushroom and sage pot pie stay out before it needs refrigeration?
implicit_anchors: Tomorrow I’ll be at the historical cabin from 8 a.m. to 3 p.m. helping the apprentices.
The cabin refrigerator is unplugged, and the microwave may not be working.
I’m trying to use up leftovers rather than spend more on food this week.

proactive_subtasks.task: Give the safe room-temperature limit for cooked pot pie and the cooling/refrigeration rule for leftovers.
proactive_subtasks.logic: The user cannot decide whether the leftover is usable for the day without the food-safety time window.

proactive_subtasks.task: Identify whether the pot pie is suitable for that site as-is and suggest a safer transport method if the user still wants to bring it.
proactive_subtasks.logic: The lack of reliable refrigeration or reheating changes whether the leftover can be used safely during the work period.

proactive_subtasks.task: Offer one or two low-cost fallback meal options that use the same leftovers or common pantry items already at home.
proactive_subtasks.logic: If the pot pie cannot stay safe under site conditions, the hidden goal still requires a budget-conscious way to avoid buying food.

proactive_subtasks.task: Provide a simple night-before and morning-of packing timeline.
proactive_subtasks.logic: Safe use of leftovers depends on cooling, storage, and transport order, not just the maximum time at room temperature.

ideal_assistant_trajectory.description: Answer that a cooked pot pie should not sit at room temperature for more than about 2 hours, or 1 hour if conditions are very warm, and note that leftovers should be cooled and refrigerated promptly.
Point out that the user may need a food option that stays safe without depending on onsite appliances, and ask whether an insulated bag, ice packs, or a vacuum thermos is available.
ideal_assistant_trajectory.grounding: The cabin refrigerator is unplugged, and the microwave may not be working -> the user has an unstated need for a meal plan that does not rely on reliable cold storage or reheating at the site.

ideal_assistant_trajectory.description: Conclude that bringing the pot pie loose for the full workday is not the best fit, and proactively suggest either packing a chilled portion with ice packs or repurposing the filling into a hot thermos meal so the leftovers can still be used without buying separate food.
ideal_assistant_trajectory.grounding: Tomorrow I’ll be at the historical cabin from 8 a.m. to 3 p.m. helping the apprentices + The cabin refrigerator is unplugged, and the microwave may not be working + I’m trying to use up leftovers rather than spend more on food this week -> the user needs a safe, low-cost way to turn existing leftovers into a worksite meal under limited storage conditions.

ideal_assistant_trajectory.description: Add a short checklist for tonight and tomorrow morning, such as refrigerating the portion overnight, reheating fully before using a thermos, or packing it straight from the refrigerator with frozen packs before the 8 a.m. departure.
ideal_assistant_trajectory.grounding: Tomorrow I’ll be at the historical cabin from 8 a.m. to 3 p.m. helping the apprentices -> provide a forward-looking prep timeline tied to the departure time and length of the day away from home.

culinary_persona_scenarios.persona_alignment_check: All proactive subtasks stay within ordinary home food-safety guidance, use existing leftovers or low-cost equipment, and do not conflict with the persona’s budgeting or professional limits.
